payload.title: Knowledge runs only create concepts: never change one that exists
payload.description:
Ryan 2026-11-03: a knowledge run, and any other automated writer, never changes a concept node that already exists. Get or create: if the node is missing create it; if it exists leave it alone; either way write the associations to it. People's edits in the wiki must survive every run.

## The rule, in one place

New module `src/papyrus_content/semantic_node_writes.py`, used by every automated writer of `SemanticNode`:

- `IDENTITY_FIELDS`: displayName, description, aliases, nodeKind, nodeKey, status, and everything else not derived. Never changed on an existing node by a machine.
- `DERIVED_FIELDS`: authorityScore, authorityRank, acceptedReferenceMentionCount, distinctSourceKindCount, relationCount (and updatedAt with them). These are numbers worked out from the graph, and a machine may keep updating them, as a partial update naming only those fields, never a write of the whole row.
- A function that takes an existing row and what a machine wants and returns the patch or nothing.

Exceptions, both kept and specified in Gherkin: (a) a `generated` node may move to `accepted` when a published Story's front matter names it (`plan_front_matter` today), because otherwise those concepts never become public; only from `generated`, never from `rejected`. (b) the acceptance mark in `changeReason` on a node that same front-matter path created. Report in your hand-back anything else you believe needs an exception, and do not add it without saying so.

## Writers to change (read each; these came from a search, so confirm by reading)

1. `src/papyrus_content/analysis_graph.py`: the most serious. `_build...` around line 240 writes nodes with `nodeKey` `extractor:snapshot:node`, so every import mints a new node for the same concept, and around line 380 it marks the nodes of earlier imports `versionState: superseded`. On Machines on Machines 7,662 nodes are superseded with an importRunId starting `knowledge-import-knowledge`. Change it so an import resolves each node to an existing node by kind and case and white-space insensitive name or alias (reuse `NodeIndex` from `knowledge_snapshot/publish_run.py`), creates only when none matches, points its relations at the existing node, and never supersedes a node. A rejected node is never revived or linked. Leave its handling of relations as it is unless a relation would point at a node that no longer gets created; say what you did. Find out whether a knowledge run reaches this path (`analysis_commands.py`, `docs/knowledge-cloud-run.md`) and report it.
2. `src/papyrus_content/ontology_enrichment.py` around line 600: `expected = dict(node)` plus the authority numbers, written as a whole row. Change it to a partial update of DERIVED_FIELDS, so an edit made since the read is not overwritten.
3. `src/papyrus_content/knowledge_snapshot/publish_run.py`: line ~239 lacks `createOnly`; add it. Check `apply` in `knowledge_snapshot/commands.py:203`.
4. `src/papyrus_content/reference_url_text.py` around line 2245: the author node; make it create-only.
5. Read `knowledge_snapshot/entity_retype.py`, `categories_steering.py` (lines ~956, ~1103), `site_sweep.py:104`, `relevance_decisions.py:45`, `rehydration_commands.py`. Fix any automated write that can change an existing concept. Commands a person runs on purpose (retype, steering decisions, rehydration) stay as they are; list them in your report. Classifier nodes are not concepts.

Also check `knowledge_wiki/sync.py` `_plan_page`: it can UPDATE a generated wiki page. Do not change it in this ticket, but report whether a person's wiki edit to a page or node is overwritten, and how.

## Guard

A test that fails when a module other than the allowed list writes `SemanticNode` with a non-create-only record. Keep it simple: grep-style over `src/papyrus_content`, in the style of `procedures/guards/`.

## Docs and specs

`features_backend/knowledge-run-concepts.feature`, narrative and complete: a concept a person edited keeps its name, description and aliases through a run; a new mention of an existing concept writes the association and no node; a mention of an unknown concept creates it and the association; matching by alias reuses the node; a rejected concept is not revived or linked; the derived numbers update without touching anything else; two imports of one concept make one node; earlier imports are not superseded; the two exceptions. Add the rule to `docs/knowledge-base.md` and a process entry to `docs/automated-processes.md` using its template. Fix the sentence in `docs/idea-context-packs.md` that says generated concepts would be overwritten by the next run, if it is no longer true; it stays until the editing ticket lets people edit them.
